item.title: Pensacola State College closes through Saturday for Hurricane Isaias
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Pensacola State College will shut down all campus locations starting at 4 p.m. today and remain closed through Saturday, October 10, due to Hurricane Isaias, the college announced Thursday morning. The closure affects all classes, events, campus activities, and online courses. Emergency personnel will remain on campus during the closure. The…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola State College will shut down all campus locations starting at 4 p.m. today and remain closed through Saturday, October 10, due to Hurricane Isaias, the college announced Thursday morning.

The closure affects all classes, events, campus activities, and online courses. Emergency personnel will remain on campus during the closure. The college is taking the precaution as the hurricane approaches the region.

Library services are expected to resume Sunday, October 11, and will be available to students. The college will provide updates on its social media platforms, website at pensacolastate.edu, and through PSC Alert if conditions change.

item.title: DOH-Escambia Opens Special Needs Shelter at Wagner Road Location
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Florida Department of Health in Escambia County opened a Special Needs Shelter on Thursday at the Marie K. Young-Wedgewood Community Center and Park, located at 6405 Wagner Road in Pensacola. The shelter is designed to serve people with stable impairments or disabilities whose care needs go beyond basic first aid available at general shelters.…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Health in Escambia County opened a Special Needs Shelter on Thursday at the Marie K. Young-Wedgewood Community Center and Park, located at 6405 Wagner Road in Pensacola. The shelter is designed to serve people with stable impairments or disabilities whose care needs go beyond basic first aid available at general shelters.

The facility opened at 3 p.m. today and can accommodate residents whose medical requirements exceed what standard emergency shelters provide. DOH-Escambia notes that nursing staff at the location is limited, so shelter attendees are strongly encouraged to bring a caregiver. Staff will be available to assist when medical needs exceed a caregiver's training or knowledge.

Residents planning to use the shelter should arrive prepared with bedding, food and water for up to seven days, medications and medical supplies for that same period, toiletries, and clothing. Each person should plan to bring one gallon of water per day for a week-long stay. Service animals are permitted in the shelter space; other pets will be housed in a separate animal shelter area at the same location. More details about pet requirements are available on the Escambia County Emergency Management website.

item.content:encoded:
Escambia County officials announced Thursday that evacuation orders will be issued later in the day as Hurricane Isaias continues to intensify, according to Miramar News.

The orders will affect Pensacola Beach, Perdido Key, and other low-lying areas throughout the county. Residents in those zones are urged to monitor official channels for updates and prepare to leave as soon as orders are formally announced.

This is a developing situation. More details on the evacuation timeline and specific zones will be released as the day progresses. Residents should have a plan in place and monitor Escambia County emergency management for official guidance.

item.title: Santa Rosa Opens Special Needs Shelter at Milton Community Center Friday
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Florida Department of Health in Santa Rosa County will open a Special Needs Shelter beginning Friday, October 9, at 8 a.m. at the Clyde L. Gracey Community Center in Milton, located at 5629 Byrom St. The shelter is designed for people whose age, frailty, mobility, functional, or medical disability makes them vulnerable in disaster situations.…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Health in Santa Rosa County will open a Special Needs Shelter beginning Friday, October 9, at 8 a.m. at the Clyde L. Gracey Community Center in Milton, located at 5629 Byrom St.

The shelter is designed for people whose age, frailty, mobility, functional, or medical disability makes them vulnerable in disaster situations. Those eligible include individuals with pre-existing medical conditions who have been able to maintain daily living activities at home before a disaster.

Attendees should bring a caregiver with them, as nursing staff at the shelter is limited and available primarily to assist with medical needs beyond a caregiver's training. Residents should pack bedding, medications and medical supplies for seven days, non-perishable food and water (one gallon per person per day for up to a week), toiletries, and clothing. Service animals are permitted in the shelter; other pets will be housed in a separate animal shelter area at the location.

For more information about pet disaster preparedness requirements, residents can visit the Santa Rosa County website. Those with questions can contact the Florida Department of Health in Santa Rosa County at PIO.CHD57@flhealth.gov or 850-851-8929.

item.title: Milton declares local emergency, closes offices Friday ahead of Hurricane Isaias
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The City of Milton is preparing for Hurricane Isaias by declaring a state of local emergency and shutting down municipal operations Friday, October 9, according to a release from Mayor Heather Lindsay's office Thursday. All city offices will close Friday, and several services are being adjusted. Sanitation collections will run from 7 a.m. to noon,…
item.content:encoded:
The City of Milton is preparing for Hurricane Isaias by declaring a state of local emergency and shutting down municipal operations Friday, October 9, according to a release from Mayor Heather Lindsay's office Thursday.

All city offices will close Friday, and several services are being adjusted. Sanitation collections will run from 7 a.m. to noon, and residents are asked to place carts curbside early and secure them immediately after pickup. The community center is cancelling all activities beginning at 4:30 p.m. Thursday, and city parks will close Friday and remain closed until further notice. The city is also pausing late fees on utility bills for October 8–9.

Milton's Clyde L. Gracey Community Center at 5629 Byrom Street will open as a pet-friendly emergency shelter at 8 a.m. Friday, with no preregistration required. Residents should bring identification, medications, water, snacks, bedding and personal essentials. Those bringing pets need carriers, proof of vaccinations, and pet supplies; meals will not be provided. Transportation assistance to shelters is available by calling (850) 983-4636 while winds remain below tropical storm force.

City officials are coordinating with Santa Rosa County Emergency Management and urge residents to complete storm preparations, secure outdoor items, avoid flooded roads, and monitor official weather updates. For the latest information, visit miltonfl.org or the City of Milton's Facebook page.

item.content:encoded:
Pensacola International Airport will suspend commercial flight operations beginning at 10 a.m. Friday as Hurricane Isaias approaches the Gulf Coast, according to an announcement from the airport.

The closure is part of a broader preparation effort across Northwest Florida as the storm tracks toward a Gulf Coast landfall. A second airport in the region has also announced similar precautions, though specific details on that facility were not immediately available.

The 10 a.m. Friday closure gives the airport time to secure facilities and allow passengers and staff to seek shelter before conditions deteriorate. Travelers with flights scheduled during or after the closure window should contact their airlines for rebooking options.

item.content:encoded:
REGYMEN Fitness, a Pensacola-based performance fitness brand, announced plans to expand into New Zealand with nine locations, according to a company statement released Thursday. The expansion marks a significant step in the company's international growth strategy.

The first New Zealand studio is targeted for Silverdale, Auckland, with plans to open in late 2026. The company did not immediately provide a timeline for the remaining eight locations or additional details about the franchise agreements.

The expansion adds to REGYMEN Fitness's existing footprint and reflects growing interest in the performance fitness sector internationally. The company joins other fitness brands pursuing overseas franchise opportunities as the industry continues to evolve post-pandemic.

item.title: Fried: Expunged Hope Florida Report Doesn't Erase $10M Scandal
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Florida Democratic Party Chair Nikki Fried said Thursday that a court order expunging a grand jury report on the Hope Florida controversy doesn't undo the underlying facts of what she characterized as a scheme to misuse Medicaid settlement funds for political purposes. The First District Court of Appeal ruled to expunge the grand jury report,…
item.content:encoded:
Florida Democratic Party Chair Nikki Fried said Thursday that a court order expunging a grand jury report on the Hope Florida controversy doesn't undo the underlying facts of what she characterized as a scheme to misuse Medicaid settlement funds for political purposes.

The First District Court of Appeal ruled to expunge the grand jury report, which had concluded that $10 million from a Medicaid settlement was routed through a charity connected to the governor's wife and ultimately used to fund political activity. Fried's statement argues the ruling represents a legal victory for the DeSantis administration but not a factual exoneration.

"What happened in court wasn't a new investigation of those facts," Fried said in the statement. She noted that those challenging the report had their day in court while no one formally defended the grand jury's findings or presented the evidence it reviewed. Fried also highlighted that the opinion was authored by Judge Lance Neff, appointed to the appellate court by Governor DeSantis months after the grand jury issued its initial report.

Fried reiterated questions about why the $10 million was set aside from the settlement, why it moved into political organizations, and why those involved fought to keep the report from public view. "This is what unchecked power looks like after decades of one-party rule in Tallahassee," she said.

item.title: Health Department Offices Close Across Escambia, Santa Rosa Counties as Severe Weather Approaches
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Florida Department of Health in both Escambia and Santa Rosa counties announced office closures Thursday in preparation for severe weather impacts expected to hit the region. DOH-Escambia offices are closing at 2 p.m. today, October 8, and will remain shut until further notice. In Santa Rosa County, the midway office closed earlier today,…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Health in both Escambia and Santa Rosa counties announced office closures Thursday in preparation for severe weather impacts expected to hit the region.

DOH-Escambia offices are closing at 2 p.m. today, October 8, and will remain shut until further notice. In Santa Rosa County, the midway office closed earlier today, while all other DOH-Santa Rosa locations will close Friday, October 9, and remain closed pending conditions improvement.

Residents seeking emergency information can contact the State Assistance Information Line at 800-342-3557 or visit the Florida Division of Emergency Management website at floridadisaster.org. Escambia County residents can also check myescambia.com, while Santa Rosa County residents can visit santarosa.fl.gov/974/Emergency-Management for local emergency resources, shelter information, and preparedness guidance. Anyone experiencing a medical emergency should call 911.

item.title: State Court Expunges Hope Florida Grand Jury Report on Medicaid Settlement
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A Florida appellate court has ordered the expungement of a grand jury report that alleged $10 million from a Medicaid settlement was misappropriated by Hope Florida, according to reporting on the ruling issued Wednesday. The expungement order comes after the report's contents had already been publicly leaked and covered extensively by media…
item.content:encoded:
A Florida appellate court has ordered the expungement of a grand jury report that alleged $10 million from a Medicaid settlement was misappropriated by Hope Florida, according to reporting on the ruling issued Wednesday.

The expungement order comes after the report's contents had already been publicly leaked and covered extensively by media outlets. The grand jury investigation centered on how settlement funds were handled by the organization.

While the court's directive removes the official record, the earlier public disclosure means the allegations have remained in circulation. The ruling reflects legal proceedings around the handling of the grand jury findings but does not reverse the prior media coverage of the report's claims.

item.title: Century outreach teams seek homeless residents ahead of hurricane
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Two Escambia County organizations are launching an emergency outreach effort today to locate people experiencing homelessness in Century and transport them to shelter before hurricane conditions arrive. Opening Doors and Str8 Up Leadership Academy are coordinating the initiative, with Executive Director Bruce Cody and Pastor Evelyn Deterville…
item.content:encoded:
Two Escambia County organizations are launching an emergency outreach effort today to locate people experiencing homelessness in Century and transport them to shelter before hurricane conditions arrive.

Opening Doors and Str8 Up Leadership Academy are coordinating the initiative, with Executive Director Bruce Cody and Pastor Evelyn Deterville leading teams across the Century community starting at noon Thursday. The effort aims to ensure vulnerable residents have safe shelter as weather deteriorates.

The outreach represents a coordinated response between local nonprofits and community leadership to address immediate safety concerns during severe weather. Both organizations have been active in providing services to Escambia County's homeless population.

item.title: Hurricane Warning Issued for Escambia County as Isaias Approaches
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A hurricane warning is now in effect for Escambia County and much of the northern Gulf Coast as Hurricane Isaias moves toward the region. The National Weather Service warns of damaging winds, heavy rainfall, flooding, and the possibility of isolated tornadoes as the storm approaches. Isaias initially developed as a tropical storm early Wednesday…
item.content:encoded:
A hurricane warning is now in effect for Escambia County and much of the northern Gulf Coast as Hurricane Isaias moves toward the region. The National Weather Service warns of damaging winds, heavy rainfall, flooding, and the possibility of isolated tornadoes as the storm approaches.

Isaias initially developed as a tropical storm early Wednesday morning before intensifying into a hurricane late Wednesday night. The strengthening system is expected to bring significant impacts to the area, with residents urged to prepare for the severe weather threat.

Local officials and emergency management are monitoring the storm's track closely. Residents in Escambia County should secure loose outdoor items, stock up on supplies, and review evacuation plans if they live in flood-prone or coastal areas. Updates on the hurricane's path and timing are expected as the system continues its approach.

item.title: Weather forces rash of Escambia County sports cancellations and rescheduling
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A stretch of poor weather has forced the cancellation or postponement of multiple sporting events across Escambia County, according to North Escambia. High school football games originally scheduled for Friday have been moved to Thursday night. West Florida High School's game has been pushed back to a date to be announced later. At the college…
item.content:encoded:
A stretch of poor weather has forced the cancellation or postponement of multiple sporting events across Escambia County, according to North Escambia.

High school football games originally scheduled for Friday have been moved to Thursday night. West Florida High School's game has been pushed back to a date to be announced later.

At the college level, UWF's home football game against Northwestern State set for Saturday has been canceled entirely. A weekend baseball tournament at Molino Ballpark has also been scrubbed due to the weather.

The specific weather threat and updated game times were not detailed in available reports. Fans are advised to check with their schools and teams for the latest scheduling information.
